transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2025-05-07 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Anya (Redwood SE), Ryan (CSM), Sam (Acuity Head of ML), Priya (Platform), Ethan (SRE), Lina (Data Ops)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in for throughput optimization. Main focus: continuous batching, setting concurrency targets, dealing with queueing/backpressure seen during burst tests.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining; quick roll call before we jump in
00:06 Sam: yep Sam here, Priya, Ethan, Lina are on
00:10 Priya: here
00:12 Ethan: here
00:15 Lina: present
00:20 Jordan: Jordan from Redwood SE, Anya also on; we'll run thru the perf numbers and tuning suggestions
00:28 Maya: agenda two things review last run, then propose config changes for continuous batching and concurrency targets, time for q's at end
00:40 Sam: sounds good we mostly want to see where the bottleneck is \u0014 we saw token latency spikes at 95th percentile when qps hit 1.2k in burst tests
00:55 Jordan: yeah we pulled the traces, quick note transcription: a bunch of the service names got munged in the logs but it's fine, the KV cache hits were stable at 86% so not the culprit
01:12 Anya: right; the main pattern is queue buildup at the frontend autoscaler \u0014 requests pile up during bursts, autoscaler spins up but there's a lag, and then backend GPU queues get saturated causing head-of-line blocking
01:30 Priya: can you clarify autoscaler? is that GKE HPA or your Redwood front-end scaler?
01:35 Jordan: it's the Redwood request router/autoscaler tier \u0014 it proxies into the dedicated pool. We observed request concurrency limit per worker set to 8 which is too high for our workload; when 8 heavy requests hit, latency for subsequent ones jumps
01:52 Ethan: to confirm, our client sends 50 concurrent connections during the test, each multiplexing requests; we saw queuing in nginx as well, so there's some network layer too
02:08 Maya: ok so two levers: continuous batching config (batch size ceilings, batch timeout), and concurrency caps per worker + queue depth tuning at the front
02:25 Sam: what did last week's perf spreadsheet show? can you summarize numbers?
02:30 Jordan: sure: baseline single-worker throughput ~220 rps for the model variant we used (gptx-8q), with batching enabled we saw aggregate throughput up to ~1.0k rps across 6 workers; however p95 token latency jumped from 180ms to 420ms under bursts because queue depth spiked
02:50 Anya: also noticed CPU at the router was peaking then dropping as new workers came up \u0014 so autoscaler cooldown and provision time add to the effective queueing window
03:05 Priya: so is a lower concurrency per worker better? seems counterintuitive: fewer concurrency -> less throughput per worker usually
03:12 Jordan: yes it's a tradeoff \u0014 for our workload shorter sequences and variable batchability, setting concurrency to 4 improved latency tail because batches were formed faster and less head-of-line blocking. Overall throughput stayed similar when we also increased max batch size and enabled prefix caching aggressively
03:30 Sam: how does continuous batching timeout play in here? we currently have 25ms batch timeout in prod-like config
03:36 Anya: 25ms is conservative; for Acuity's distribution (many short prompts, median length ~60 tokens) moving to 40ms with larger max batch size helps assemble more tokens into fewer model calls while still meeting p50 latency needs
03:50 Ethan: tradeoff is p95 could increase though right?
03:53 Jordan: depending on concurrency; if you pair 40ms timeout with concurrency cap 4 and queue_size 120 we saw p95 at ~310ms vs 420ms previously \u0014 so it's an overall win in our runs
04:12 Lina: can you share the config you tested? we need to apply similar in our staging cluster to reproduce
04:18 Maya: yes we'll send the exact config; high level: concurrency_per_worker=4, batch_timeout_ms=40, max_batch_tokens=1024, queue_size=120, enable_prefix_cache=true
04:34 Priya: what's the effect on GPU occupancy? we worry about underutilization with lower concurrency
04:40 Jordan: GPU occupancy dips a bit per worker but because you get faster turnaround you can scale horizontally more predictably; net qps improved because end-to-end latency reduced and clients retry/backoff less
04:55 Sam: earlier you mentioned KV cache hits were 86% \u0014 is there room to improve there?
05:00 Anya: maybe; we recommended boosting prefix cache retention and increasing cache size on the model nodes by 25% for this POC; we can send guidance and projected memory impact
05:14 Priya: ok please add numbers about memory footprint
05:17 Jordan: will do in the spreadsheet
05:20 Maya: another item: network egress and firewall rules \u0014 Ethan you saw nginx queuing; do you want us to run a synthetic test that pins connection patterns?
05:29 Ethan: yes we'll run the synthetic that mimics our client multiplexing; also we'll open tcp keepalive tuning as part of the test
05:36 Sam: what about queueing at the client side \u0014 we use an internal SDK that retries; could be amplifying the traffic
05:42 Anya: good call, if client retries with no jitter it exacerbates bursts; adding exponential backoff + jitter reduced observed burst factor by ~18% in our sim
05:55 Priya: any thoughts on target concurrency for go/no-go? what number are we aiming for?
06:00 Jordan: for the POC ramp we propose fixed concurrency target of 4 per worker and target aggregate qps 800 sustained with 1.5k burst headroom; that's aligned with your business SLOs we discussed last week
06:15 Sam: does Redwood have autoscaling knobs to provide faster scale-up? cooldowns are big contributor right now
06:21 Anya: we can shorten scale-up cooldown and pre-warm instances during expected peaks; also a warm pool option (reserved spare workers) reduces spin-up latency. Those are available in Dedicated configs
06:35 Sam: cost impact? reserved warm pool will add cost
06:38 Maya: yes we'll estimate cost delta in the spreadsheet; typically warm pool is cheaper than underprovisioning because it avoids SLA violations and retries
06:48 Priya: can you walk through the benchmark steps we'll run this week?
06:52 Jordan: quick runbook: 1) deploy updated config to staging, 2) run client with 8 concurrent clients for 20 minutes ramping to target qps, 3) capture router and worker traces + GPU metrics, 4) run burst tests with sudden 2x traffic to measure scale-up, 5) collect logs and upload to our secure share
07:20 Ethan: what telemetry fields do you need exactly?
07:25 Jordan: router qlen, per-worker in-flight count, batch sizes histogram, batch timeout histogram, kv cache hit ratio, gpu utilization, p50/p95 token latency, request ingress qps, nginx queue metrics
07:36 Lina: we'll try to map those fields to our current telemetry; some are missing but we can add tracing points
07:44 Maya: timeline: we want the benchmark results by Mon 2025-05-12; SE deep-dive Wed 2025-05-14 at 10am PT if that works for you
07:55 Sam: works for us
07:57 Priya: works
08:00 Jordan: quick note on an alternate approach: if you want to optimize for cost rather than latency, we can try higher concurrency + larger batches but that increases tail latency; we didn't push that here because Acuity prioritized tail for UX
08:18 Sam: yes tail matters for our clinicians; so we'll go with the p95 improvements route
08:22 Maya: any blockers from your side for the run?
08:25 Priya: just getting the staging config change approved; should be ok by tomorrow morning
08:30 Ethan: we'll open firewall egress rule for the test and attach the nginx logs to the share
08:35 Maya: perfect. i'll share the config, the perf spreadsheet, and a runbook after this call. Jordan will run the deep-dive.
08:45 Sam: thanks team, appreciate the concrete plan
08:50 Maya: recap of action items and owners in the chat \u0014 please ack in CRM and we'll close the loop
08:58 All: thanks, bye

Post-call notes:
- Attachments to be uploaded: perf_spreadsheet_may07.csv, batching_config_v1.json, runbook_poc_throughput.md (links to be shared in follow up)
- Risks: warm pool cost vs. scale-up lag; client retry pattern amplifying bursts; some telemetry gaps in customer staging
